slides.subtitle: JobHub research findings
slides.lead: A reading deck before product analysis
slides.footnote: Rounds 00–02 · Research reviewed 18 October 2026
slides.notes: This briefing distils the research already in the repository. It introduces no new participant evidence. The expanded Round 02 pass has independent review. Its findings inform discussion, while product scope and platform remain open.

slides.title: What the research suggests
slides.lead: Useful support may reduce uncertainty and repeated effort.

items.heading: People need help judging opportunities
items.text: Actual duties, working conditions and verified experience matter alongside job titles.

items.heading: Preparation includes checking and recovery
items.text: Re-entry, corrections, scheduling and unfinished work add to the writing itself.

items.heading: Truthful reuse is worth testing
items.text: Real examples can support resumes and interview practice without invented achievements.

items.heading: The simplest useful workflow remains open
items.text: Manual documents, peers and career coaching offer meaningful alternatives.

slides.footnote: Synthesis of reported mechanisms. Their prevalence and JobHub benefit remain unmeasured.
slides.notes: Round 02 F01–F10. Public accounts, guidance and internal process evidence support investigating these mechanisms. They do not rank user demand or establish a preferred initial segment.

slides.title: Pain across the job-search journey
slides.lead: Preparation work and employer-controlled delays can overlap.
rows: Repeated tailoring, parsed-field corrections and re-entry
Leave, scheduling, assessments and uncertain round counts
slides.footnote: Accounts describe mechanisms. This pass did not measure their frequency or total time cost.
slides.notes: Practices P01/P02/P05/P10/P12. P01 is a retrospective retail-to-healthcare-operations story. P02 is a Singapore forum discussion including non-tech interview burden. Keep separate people's experiences separate. The same sources include positive outcomes and successful alternatives.

slides.title: Red flags become verification questions
slides.lead: Specific checks make concerns more useful.
rows: Can the organisation independently confirm the contact and vacancy?
What work will I do, and how will success be assessed?
What is the deadline, assessment scope and reason?
What explains the hiring history, expectations and working conditions?
slides.footnote: Research-derived guidance. A phrase, repeated listing or polished website cannot establish employer intent.
slides.notes: Domain D01/D02/D05/D08/D09 and videos V01–V05. Distinguish authenticity concerns from personal fit and unclear conditions. Some warning signs may have legitimate explanations, including scarce skills, contracting, delayed headcount or multi-location hiring. ScamShield provides independently checkable authenticity guidance.

slides.title: Job fit needs several kinds of evidence
slides.lead: A low keyword score can hide relevant experience.

items.heading: Demonstrated experience
items.text: Which real tasks or outcomes support the requirement?

items.heading: Transferable skills
items.text: How does that experience apply in the new setting?

items.heading: A real gap or missing information
items.text: Does the person lack the skill, or does the record need clarification?

items.heading: Essential criteria and personal conditions
items.text: Verify requirements, shifts, location and constraints before judging suitability.

slides.footnote: Research-derived guidance. No validated fit score or individual eligibility assessment resulted from this research.
slides.notes: Domain D03/D10/D12 and internal I03/I04/I13. WSG permits application despite a low portal match score. This does not waive current role-specific licensing or eligibility rules. No such role-specific legal assessment was conducted.

slides.title: Pay comparisons need a common basis
slides.lead: Market pay, the full offer and personal priorities answer different questions.
rows: Role, scope, level, location and reference date
Basic pay, allowances and hours on a consistent basis
Bonus, commission, equity, vesting and eligibility
Leave, benefits, shifts, location and contract terms
slides.footnote: Research-derived guidance. MOM's 2025 wage data provide context without determining an individual's entitlement.
slides.notes: Domain D04/D05/D06/D11. MOM definitions exclude different components from basic and gross wages, with survey population limits. Basic/gross figures are before employee CPF and income-tax deductions. Equity and variable pay should not be treated as guaranteed recurring cash. No personal salary calculation was made.

slides.title: Negotiation depends on the opportunity
slides.lead: A prepared choice can include accepting, countering or declining.

columns.heading: Preparation
items: Find comparable evidence for the role
Clarify what can change in the package

slides.footnote: Research-derived guidance. No universal uplift or risk-free negotiation script is established.
slides.notes: Domain D06/D07/D11 and internal I08. NUS guidance, a US-tech field experiment and a Singapore forum account offer different levels of evidence. The internal strategist's categorical timing/counter rules should not become universal JobHub defaults. D07 independent recheck timed out, as recorded in review.

slides.title: Truthful tailoring starts with real facts
slides.lead: Research-derived guidance uses fictional examples. Titles, dates and metrics stay factual.
rows: New role's technical tasks may differ
Describe the actual records and tools used
State the support provided and real outcome
slides.footnote: Accounts report benefits from both tailoring and resume reuse. Neither approach is established as best.
slides.notes: Illustrative examples are newly authored fictional cases, not user research or the owner's career claims. Practices P07/P10, internal I04/I05 and videos V06/V07 support selecting relevant examples and checking changes. Do not convert a suggested metric or project into an established candidate achievement.

items: Rehearse aloud with a peer, coach or tool

slides.footnote: Research-derived guidance. No calibrated readiness score or hiring-effect estimate for JobHub exists.
slides.notes: P08/P09/P12, I06/I07, V08. Some advice comes from graduate/international contexts. The internal process prescribes attempts, retries and debriefs, but this review did not inspect completed private interview attempts. Scheduling and excessive employer rounds remain separate burdens.

slides.title: AI assistance also creates checking work
slides.lead: A useful evaluation includes the effort after generation.

columns.heading: Checks that remain
items: Source accuracy, freshness and missing details

slides.footnote: Some people use human or manual alternatives. This pass does not rank ChatGPT, Claude or other tools.
slides.notes: P03/P05/P06/P07/P09 and C01/C02. Included experiments report bounded outcomes for different interventions. This research conducted no original provider comparison or JobHub net-effort test. P06's file diagnosis was not independently verified. V09 supplies a weak narrated tutorial, not a verified successful application.

slides.title: Different AI interventions, different outcomes
slides.lead: Primary studies provide useful findings with specific transfer limits.
rows: Higher hiring probability, with no detected employer-satisfaction loss
An online labour-market experiment, not a current chatbot comparison
Generative drafts for employer job posts
Less employer writing time and more posts, without a discernible increase in matches
A different intervention in an online labour market
slides.footnote: Distinct experiments with overlapping authorship. Neither measures JobHub benefit.
slides.notes: C01: arXiv abstract submitted 2023-01-19, algorithmic resume-writing assistance. C02: author-hosted More, but Worse working paper, 2026-09-04 revision, employer job-post generation. C01 reports an 8% relative hiring-probability increase in its setting. C02 reports reduced employer drafting time and no discernible net matching increase; its welfare accounting is model-based. Authors and intervention details overlap in provenance, but these are different experiments, not replications or a provider ranking. No JobHub or Singapore net-effort effect follows.

slides.title: The existing Job Hunt process
slides.lead: A detailed personal workflow provides useful patterns and specific weaknesses.

columns.heading: Documented strengths
items: A factual authority for career claims

columns.heading: Weaknesses and open checks
items: Current operation and coordination effort untested

slides.footnote: One owner's documented process. Private resumes, contracts and correspondence stayed outside the deck.
slides.notes: Internal I01–I16. The reviewer inspected 25 process files and five historical artifacts with sanitized references. Older positive transport statuses sometimes accompanied loading/error content, while later artifacts had structured results. Neither observation proves current end-to-end success or failure. No private source files were changed.

slides.title: What the videos added
slides.lead: Ten caption reviews broadened the questions and examples.

items.heading: Supplied red-flag discussions
items.text: Clarification questions, interview burden and legitimate alternative explanations

items.heading: Additional resume and AI tutorials
items.text: Fact-first drafting and inspection of changes to titles or achievements

items.heading: Interview and compensation material
items.text: Manual story notebooks, spoken practice and questions for comparing compensation

items.heading: Evidence limits
items.text: Advice dominates. Popularity and repeated statistics do not establish outcomes.

slides.footnote: Caption analysis only. Salary clip: 2020 international raise advice. No listening or screen verification.
slides.notes: V01–V10 span eight creator families. All five supplied captions and five additional captions were reviewed. Six additional candidate URL checks included one wrong-case failure. Three manual-track and seven automatic-track captures in total. The extra salary source is old international raise advice. Video statistics were excluded from quantitative synthesis.

slides.title: Privacy is part of the workflow
slides.lead: Reusing career evidence can also concentrate personal information.

items.heading: Necessary information
items.text: Which facts does this task actually require?

items.heading: Disclosure
items.text: What will a tool, provider or third party receive?

items.heading: Access and retention
items.text: Who can read the record, and how long should it remain?

items.heading: Correction and control
items.text: Can the person inspect, change and remove what the workflow uses?

slides.footnote: These are design questions. Current provider policies and implemented controls remain unreviewed.
slides.notes: F12, P07 and I14. Independent review required clearer privacy coverage. Use fictional data for the first proposed comparison. No provider-policy audit, access-control test or deletion-enforcement test took place.

slides.title: Earlier product and development research
slides.lead: The baseline work offers directions to examine after reading the findings.

items.heading: Existing alternatives already overlap
items.text: General assistants, career tools, manual records and human support deserve comparison.

items.heading: Small development slices may suit the uncertainty
items.text: Use a short behaviour brief, narrow implementation and independent verification.

items.heading: Gherkin examples can clarify behaviour
items.text: Given/When/Then examples clarify behaviour. Running them as tests remains optional.

items.heading: Ownership requires understanding
items.text: The owner should explain data flow, failure handling, tests and recovery.

slides.footnote: Round 00 recommendations. No local productivity benchmark, stack choice or competitive advantage is proven.
slides.notes: These are earlier desk-research proposals, not refreshed current product comparisons. Do not repeat historical configuration observations as current facts. Product usefulness, method speed, commercial demand and provider superiority remain unvalidated.

slides.title: Questions the research leaves open
slides.lead: The evidence supports mechanisms more strongly than rankings or outcomes.

items.heading: Who needs which help most?
items.text: Prevalence, comparative burden, demand and willingness to pay remain unknown.

items.heading: What works across different contexts?
items.text: Local accessibility, frontline work, languages and cover-letter practices need more evidence.

items.heading: Does assistance reduce total effort?
items.text: JobHub timing, correction, recovery and hiring outcomes have not been tested.

items.heading: Which product decisions follow?
items.text: Initial scope, platform, stack, automation and privacy choices remain open.

slides.footnote: English-language graduate, office and technology perspectives remain prominent. All ten objectives have findings or gaps.
slides.notes: Bounded public evidence cannot substitute for direct participant research or product evaluation. This owner currently has no direct user access. The exact phone-to-laptop sequence and operational effectiveness of the personal workflow remain unresolved.

items: One fictional job and verified fictional career facts
Compare assisted selection with a manual document
Use identical inputs and an interrupted return

columns.heading: What to examine
items: Clarity of fit, gaps and explanations
Ability to explain the prepared content

slides.footnote: A proposal for discussion. Owner testing can assess logic and effort while demand remains open.
slides.notes: No new experiment has been executed. Keep interviews and compensation as separate later task options to avoid obscuring what helps. Compare frontline/shift and career-change cases separately. Before proceeding, discuss which uncertainty matters most and what result would change direction.
